brief: ING argues a break above 5% on the US 10yr Treasury yield is near-inevitable, driven primarily by higher real yields, with fiscal and issuance concerns the dominant force. Higher oil prices and rising inflation expectations add pressure, while AI productivity driven real rate gains are present but overshadowed by these more negative factors. The 10yr yield is above 4.9% (real yield 2.5%, breakeven 2.4%, both rising). Thursday's PPI (5.4%, broadly as expected) and low jobless claims did not themselves drive the move. ING treats the data as an excuse for yields to rise further. Long-end SOFR pricing implies the market expects two to three Fed rate hikes. Wednesday's tripling of long-end buybacks failed to calm rates: the 30yr yield and 30yr SOFR rose together, which ING reads as the market pricing higher hike odds rather than a bond-positive signal. Pressure builds until hikes, fiscal discipline, or a break occurs. ING treats 5% as only a 50bp concession above its 4-4.5% neutral range, not calling for 6% but not ruling it out. Relief comes only once inflation cools and a 2027 rate-cut discount builds. ING calls the rest of 2026 a dangerous gauntlet.
